messages.subject: --maxTime and --parallel
parts:
Hi !

I'm playing with irace and I have 2 questions.

1) If I want to run (as many as possible) tests with irace for, lets say, 600 seconds in my computer, should I use --maxTime 600 ?  I specified this options and the test took much more (even if individual executions where quite fast, it was a test on just 3 small instances) (took 620 minutes). Is this options for an individual execution ?  If yes how do I specify the maximum time for the whole set of tests ? I know that I can set a budget of number executions, but it is only feasible for me usually to specify a budget of wall clock computing time.

BTW: in the first explanation of maxTime there is no information if it is on seconds:
maxTime (--max-time): the total maximum execution time of the target algorithm. Notethat you must provide either maxTime or maxExperiments.

2) parallel (mult-core) execution:
I included   parallel=5 in my scenario file, but checking my CPU usage only one or two cores are being used in general. My (toy) test has only three instances but the parameter space is large, I would expect a larger CPU usage.

Thanks a lot !

Haroldo

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: --maxTime and --parallel
parts:
Hi Haroldo and welcome to the group,

1) --maxTime specifies the total time taken by the runs of the target algorithm (as reported by target-runner). However, the actual wall-clock time could be more or less depending on whether irace itself requires more time, the load of the machine, irace is waiting for IO because of network communications, hard-drives, large files, or the target-runner script is actually taking more time than it is reporting to irace (this happens if the target-runner is doing many more things than running the solver). A difference of 620 minutes for 600 seconds sounds very strange. I wonder where the extra time comes from (this should be easy to see by looking at the output of irace, since it tells you the wall-clock time taken by the target-runner and gives timestamps for various irace steps). If you send me the output printed by irace (either via private email or here), I may be able to pin-point where time is being spent (if you re-run with --debug-level 4 (debugLevel=4 in the scenario file), this will give me more info to work with.

Nevertheless, we could add an option to specify the wall-clock time as one possible termination criteria. The downside is that wall-clock time is a poor measure of computational effort as it is too sensitive to system load, implementation details of the tuner, hardware hipcups, target-runner extra work, etc. Hence, if you want to report the effort of tuning, either number of runs or CPU-time required by the target algorithm would better.

I have fixed the user-guide for the next release. Thanks for pointing this out.

2) That is very strange. The only reason I can imagine is that the budget is small and less than 5 configurations are launched per instance (the number of instances does not matter). Could you share (either via private email or here) the output printed by irace in this case?

Cheers,

Manuel.
